'''Formats''' are the card pools and deck rules that Star Wars CCG games and tournaments are played under. The tables below list every format the wiki documents, where each one comes from, and how many recorded tournaments used it. Each format has its own page with its card pool, history and tournaments. What "format" and "constructed" meant to Decipher and the Players Committee over the years is told in [[History of Star Wars CCG formats]].

== How to read this page ==

* '''Four sources.''' A format can come from [[Decipher]] (1995–2002), from the [[Players Committee]] (PC, 2002–), from the PC's [[GEMP]] server, or only from this wiki's own GEMP at [https://play.swccg.com/ play.swccg.com].<ref name="play">[https://play.swccg.com/ play.swccg.com], GEMP. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009095947/https://play.swccg.com/ Internet Archive].</ref> Many formats belong to more than one: the 2000 World Championship pool, [[Premiere - Death Star II]], is also a GEMP format on both servers.
* '''Historical card pools are named for what was legal.''' Decipher did not name its constructed pools: each new expansion simply became legal, and the Players Committee likewise points players to the latest pool. But the game played at the 1999 World Championship is not the game of 2001, so the wiki names each period's pool after the last set it contains: ''Premiere - X'' means every Decipher set from [[Premiere]] through X; ''Premiere - Original VSn'' adds the Players Committee's original Virtual Sets 1–n (2002–2009 slips), which are not the post-2014 ''Virtual Set n''. These names let a reader rebuild and replay a deck as it was legal at the time.
* '''Fixed formats keep their originator's name.''' A format whose definition never changed (a sealed product, a closed environment) uses Decipher's or the PC's own wording, with other names noted on its page: [[Death Star II Closed Environment]], [[First Anthology Sealed]].
* '''(Modified)''' means the same card pool with a ban list.

== Decipher era (1995–2002) ==

Era hub: [[Decipher era]]. Decipher's sanctioned constructed play used every printed set legal on the event day, so the pool grew with each expansion; its events were described as ''Constructed Deck'' or ''Sealed Deck'' rather than by a named card pool, and "Open" meant an event anyone could enter (see [[History of Star Wars CCG formats]]).

=== Decipher's special formats ===

* [[Death Star II Closed Environment]] — Endor and Death Star II cards plus the Death Star II Starter Deck reprints (2000); also called Battle of Endor Environment (Players Committee)
* [[Episode I Closed Environment]] — only cards with the Episode I icon (2001 – 2002); also called Type II (players), Episode I Only Environment
* [[First Anthology Sealed]] — one First Anthology box per player (1997)
* [[Sealed Deck]] — one unopened Premiere starter deck per player (later any starter plus named packs); 40-card decks (1996 – 2002; 2015 (AFG)); also called Decipher Sealed Deck Tournament Format (1999), Premiere Sealed (Players Committee)
* [[Enhanced Format Sealed Deck]] — one Official Tournament Sealed Deck per player; 40-card decks (1998 – 2015 (AFG)); also called OTSD Sealed (Players Committee)
* [[OTSD Booster Draft]] — one Official Tournament Sealed Deck per player; boosters drafted, 18 premiums kept; 40-card decks (1999 – 2015 (AFG)); also called OTSD Booster Draft Format (Decipher, 2001)
* [[EPP Overdrive]] — one Enhanced Premiere pack per player; 30-card decks; 15-minute games (1999 – 2015 (AFG)); also called EPP Overdrive Sealed Deck Format (Decipher, 2001)
* [[Endor Draft]] — 6 Endor packs per player; 40-card decks (1999 – 2015 (AFG)); also called Endor Draft Tournament (Decipher)
* [[Death Star II Booster Draft]] — 3 Endor and 3 Death Star II boosters per player; 40-card decks (Decipher) (2000 – 2002; 2015 (AFG)); also called Death Star II Closed Environment Booster Draft, Death Star II Sealed Booster Draft, Death Star II/Endor Draft, Endor/Death Star II Booster Draft Format (Decipher, first name)
* [[Death Star II Sealed-Deck Starter Format]] — one Death Star II pre-constructed starter deck (60 cards) per player (2000 –; 2015 (AFG)); also called Endor/Death Star II Sealed-Deck Starter Format (Decipher, first name), Death Star II Sealed (Players Committee)
* [[Reflections Booster Draft]] — 3 Reflections boosters and an Enhanced Premiere pack (Decipher, 2000); 4 Reflections, Reflections II or Reflections III boosters plus six battleground locations (Players Committee) (2000 – 2015 (AFG)); also called Reflections Sealed Booster Draft (DecipherCon 2000)
* [[Constructed Deck]] — every released card; one Light Side and one Dark Side 60-card deck (1996 – 2002); also called The Decipher System (1996), Swiss (1998), Decipher Swiss format (1999), Standard Constructed Deck (2001)
* [[Junior Constructed Deck]] — the constructed pool; players 14 and younger; 40-card decks (1999 rules) (1998 – 2001); also called Junior Swiss (1998), Decipher Junior Tournament Format (1999)
* [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck (format)]] — one Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck box per player; 40-card decks; JPSD ability rule (2000 –); also called JPSD, Jabba's Palace Sealed (GEMP), JP Sealed (Players Committee GEMP)
* [[Japanese Sealed Deck]] — Japanese Premiere starter, 1 Premiere and 3 A New Hope Japanese boosters (2000) (1999 – 2000); also called Japanese Sealed
* [[Easy Come, Easy Go Sealed Deck]] — 3 Premiere Unlimited boosters, 2 Jabba's Palace boosters, 1 Enhanced Premiere pack; lost cards destroyed (2000)
* [[Highlander]] — the constructed pool, one copy of each card title or persona (2000); also called Highlander Constructed
* [[Kibitzing]] — the constructed pool; advice allowed during games (2000); also called Kibitzing Constructed
* [[Race for Alderaan Constructed]] — the constructed pool; deck built around a Third Anthology objective; modified win unless the objective flips (2000); also called Race for Alderaan
* [[Turning of a Skywalker Constructed]] — the constructed pool; deck built around a Death Star II objective; modified win unless the objective flips (2000); also called Turning of a Skywalker
* [[Team Event Format]] — the host event's pool; teams of 3–4 scored on their three best places (1999 – 2000); also called DecipherCon Team Challenge, DecipherCon Constructed Team Event
* [[Iron Man]] — the constructed pool; four decks each played once; lost cards destroyed (1999); also called Iron-Man Events
* [[No Such Thing As Luck]] — the constructed pool; every second game with the opponent's deck (1999)
* [[The Gauntlet: Dual Formats]] — 4 constructed games, then a 3-game OTSD sealed final for the top 8 (1999); also called The Gauntlet Dual Format
* [[Reflections II Booster Draft]] — 4 Reflections II boosters per player plus 6 battleground locations (6 per side from mid-2001); 40-card decks (2001 – 2008 (PC guide); folded into Reflections Booster Draft (AFG 2015)); also called Reflections II Sealed Deck: Booster Draft Format (Decipher rules page title), Reflections II Booster Draft Format (Decipher tournament resources)
* [[Progressive Sealed Deck]] — a sealed product ('the sealed box') plus one A New Hope booster added after each game (Akesson's report) (1999 (DecipherCon 1999))
* [[Players' Choice Sealed Deck]] — Decipher's own description of the event is not preserved (1999 (DecipherCon 1999)); also called Players Choice
* [[Allegiances: Multi-Deck Format]] — four-player constructed; Decipher's own description of the event is not preserved (1999 (DecipherCon 1999)); also called Allegiances Multi Deck Format

== Players Committee (2002–) ==

Era hubs: [[Virtual Original]], [[Virtual Legacy]], [[Virtual Modern]].<ref name="pc-home">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/ Star Wars Players Committee], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020234753/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/home.html Internet Archive].</ref> From March 2002 championship constructed added the Players Committee's Virtual Sets to the Decipher pool. Each original Virtual Set cutoff is its own format; the 2009 reorganization led to [[Legacy Open]], and the 2014 Virtual Card Reset to today's [[Open]] (the PC's ''Standard'').

=== Championship constructed ===

* [[Premiere - Original VS1]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Set 1 (from 9 March 2002); also called POVS1
* [[Premiere - Original VS2]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–2 (from 1 June 2002); also called POVS2
* [[Premiere - Original VS3]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–3 (from 20 September 2002); also called POVS3
* [[Premiere - Original VS4]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–4 (from 5 February 2003); also called POVS4
* [[Premiere - Original VS5]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–5 (from June 2003); also called POVS5
* [[Premiere - Original VS6]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–6 (from 12 January 2004); also called POVS6
* [[Premiere - Original VS7]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–7 (from 4 December 2006); also called POVS7
* [[Premiere - Original VS8]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–8 (from 4 December 2006); also called POVS8
* [[Premiere - Original VS13]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–13 (from 6 August 2007); also called POVS13
* [[Premiere - Original VS16]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–16 (from 15 August 2008); also called POVS16
* [[Premiere - Original VS17]] — every Decipher card plus original Virtual Sets 1–17 (from 6 February 2009); also called POVS17, Original Virtual Open
* [[Legacy Open]] — Decipher cards plus the pre-2014 Virtual Block cards (2009 – 2014); also called Legacy
* [[Open]] — Decipher cards plus current Virtual Sets and Defensive Shields (2014 –); also called Standard (Players Committee, from 2014)

=== Alternate formats ===

The PC's ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' and its formats pages define these.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

* [[Open (40 cards)]] — the Open pool, 40-card decks
* [[Open (45 cards)]] — the Open pool, 45-card decks
* [[Open (100 cards)]] — the Open pool, 100-card decks; also called 100 Card Deck Format
* [[Open (no shields)]] — the Open pool without Defensive Shields
* [[Open (no shields / no v-cards)]] — Decipher cards only, no Defensive Shields
* [[Open (no Episode VII)]] — the Open pool without Episode VII icon cards
* [[Classic]] — Decipher and current virtual cards, without Defensive Shield, Episode I or Maintenance icon cards
* [[Classic (no v-cards)]] — Classic with Decipher cards only; also called Classic No-V
* [[Classic (no v-cards) (Modified)]] — Decipher cards without Episode I or Maintenance icon cards, with all Reflections III Defensive Shields and their two Starting Effects (2025 –); also called Classic No V (Modified), CNVM
* [[Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)]] — Premiere through Cloud City with a ban list (2024 –); also called P-Cloud City (modified), PCCM
* [[Premiere - Reflections II (Modified)]] — Premiere through Reflections II with a ban list (2023 – 2024); also called P-Reflections II (w/ WYS and AOBS banned)
* [[Decipher Cards Only (Modified)]] — every Decipher card with a ban list (2025)
* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 3]] — every Decipher card plus current Virtual Sets 0–3
* [[Jawa Format]] — a ban list that removes the top of the power curve (2019 –)
* [[Scavenger Format]] — Decipher cards of common rarities only (Premiere – Death Star II)
* [[Utinni! (Jawas Only)]] — characters restricted to Jawas
* [[Limited Resources Format]] — Decipher cards minus the most abusive, plus some virtual cards
* [[Sealed]] — GEMP sealed league product, 40-card decks
* [[Cube]] — Watto's Chance Cube pool (45-card decks on the PC; 40 on play.swccg.com); also called Watto's Chance Cube
* [[JPOTSD Booster Draft]] — one Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck per player; boosters drafted, premiums kept (2015 (AFG))
* [[Secret Squirrel]] — one Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck per player, played as opened (2002 – 2015)
* [[Booster Draft]] — set by each draft format (1999 –)
* [[Team Tournament Formats]] — not set; two-player teams, one Dark and one Light deck (2015 (AFG))
* [[The Bith Shuffle (format)]] — the decks played in the main event, reassigned at random (2015 (AFG)); also called The Bith Shuffle

== GEMP ==

[[GEMP]] is the online client. Each GEMP format has a display name and a code; the table above gives both servers' names.<ref name="gemp">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/16168b26aa0c245d4427f58bbb023338af3cbf6b/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (billbisco/swccg-gemp, commit 16168b26), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021114513/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/billbisco/swccg-gemp/ec48dc19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022040117/https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/16168b26aa0c245d4427f58bbb023338af3cbf6b/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="pc-gemp">[https://github.com/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/blob/5e26dd19cc700adbf77de53e0d7b89720c94f03e/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021130403/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/5e26dd19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Differences from the Players Committee GEMP ===
The format list on play.swccg.com (billbisco/swccg-gemp, commit 16168b26) has 51 formats. The Players Committee format list (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19) has 37.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp">[https://github.com/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/blob/5e26dd19cc700adbf77de53e0d7b89720c94f03e/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021130403/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/5e26dd19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive].</ref> The differences are:
* Formats only on play.swccg.com: [[Anything Goes]], [[Ewok Format|Ewok]], [[Premiere - A New Hope Sealed]], [[Endor - Death Star II Sealed]], [[Reflections Sealed]], [[Episode I Sealed]], [[All Of The Jedi Sealed]], [[Novelty - Space Sealed]], [[Watto's Cube with objective packs Cube]], [[Watto's Cube with fixed pack Cube]], [[Premiere - Death Star II Draft]], [[Premiere - Virtual Set 13 Draft]], [[Premiere - Virtual Set 25 Draft]] and [[Cube v7 + Objectives Draft]].<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Cube]]: 40 cards on play.swccg.com and 45 cards in the Players Committee code.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Jabba's Palace Sealed]] (<code>jp_sealed</code>): named "Jabba's Palace Sealed" on play.swccg.com and "JP Sealed" in the Players Committee code.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Legacy Open|Legacy]]: play.swccg.com adds 18 set numbers from 1200 to 1292 and the <code>loreHeroicRule</code> setting.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
Differences in sealed league products and draft files are listed at [[GEMP sealed league products#Differences from the Players Committee GEMP|GEMP sealed league products]] and [[GEMP draft and cube products#Differences from the Players Committee GEMP|GEMP draft and cube products]].

* [[Dream Cards]] — the Open pool plus the Dream Cards set

* [[Ewok]] — Premiere – Death Star II with a long ban list (PC forum: Premiere - Death Star II (Ewok)) (2026 –); also called Ewok Format, Premiere - Death Star II (Ewok), PDS2E

* [[Endor - Death Star II Sealed]] — Endor and Death Star II product
* [[Reflections Sealed]] — Reflections product
* [[Episode I Sealed]] — Episode I product
* [[All Of The Jedi Sealed]] — All Of The Jedi product
* [[Novelty - Space Sealed]] — space-only novelty product; also called Space Sealed (Players Committee GEMP league type)
* [[Premiere - Death Star II Draft]] — Premiere – Death Star II booster draft
* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 13 Draft]] — Premiere – Virtual Set 13 booster draft
* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 25 Draft]] — Premiere – Virtual Set 25 booster draft
* [[Cube v7 + Objectives Draft]] — Cube v7 with objective packs
* [[Watto's Cube with objective packs Cube]] — Watto's Cube with objective packs
* [[Watto's Cube with fixed pack Cube]] — Watto's Cube with a fixed pack
